All three are ready. Each has the **same two saved links** — "Bookmark - Wikipedia" and "JavaScript | MDN" — and differs *only* in how you rename. Please try renaming a title in each, then tell me which felt best.

**Version A** — http://maker:4001/rename-a.html
Find the small **pencil (✎)** next to a title, click it. The title turns into an editable box right where it sits. Change the text and press Enter (or Save).

**Version B** — http://maker:4001/rename-b.html
Click the **"Rename"** button on a link. A small pop-up window opens with the title in a box. Change it and press Save.

**Version C** — http://maker:4001/rename-c.html
Just **click directly on the title text** itself — it becomes editable in place. Type your change and press Enter. (Here the title is no longer the clickable link; a small "open ↗" link visits the page instead.)

As you try them, a couple of things I'd genuinely like your read on:
- **Effort vs. safety.** Version C is the fastest (one click on the title), but because the title becomes the edit target, opening the page moves to a separate "open" link. Does that trade-off bother you, or feel fine?
- **Discoverability.** Version A's pencil and B's button are always visible; C relies on you knowing the title is clickable.

Which of the three feels like the way *you'd* want to rename — and does anything about the one you prefer still feel slightly off?
